newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria negotiates wheat deals to beat shortage.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria negotiates wheat deals to beat shortage.

text.p: Bulgaria, which needs 450,000 tonnes of wheat to fill the gap until the new crop, has sealed a deal with Argentina for 130,000 tonnes of grain, Deputy Agriculture Minister Alexander Rangelov said on Tuesday.
"The mill in Sofia will receive the first 31,000 tonnes in March," Rangelov told Reuters. He added that Bulgaria's Bulbank had guaranteed the payments.

Agriculture Minister Roumen Hristov said on Monday after talks with the U.S. ambassador that Bulgaria was negotiating an agreement under the U.S. Department of Agriculture's GSM-102 export credit guarantee programme for 130,000-150,000 tonnes of grain supplies.
Hristov said Bulgaria wanted to reschedule payments to be made over five years instead of the usual three.
Payments will be settled through a U.S. bank and will be guaranteed by Bulbank, officials said, adding that first supplies would be delivered in May at the earliest.
The United States has also stipulated that Bulgaria must pay $300,000 on an old grain loan under the PL-480 programme, Hristov said.
Rangelov said another option was to import 250,000-300,000 tonnes of wheat against futures contracts to export the same quantity of wheat from the new crop.
"The ministry has invited bidders for grain imports and will review their offers on February 28," Rangelov said.
In Brussels, European Union external relations commissioner Hans van den Broek said on Tuesday the EU would consider providing grain aid worth about two million Ecus.
Bulgaria is suffering an acute grain shortage after uncontrolled exports two years ago depleted supplies. A poor harvest last year was attributed to bad weather and a lack of funds for fertilisers.
On Monday the interim government unblocked 21,400 tonnes of wheat from the state reserves. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
